# Template: reed_frost
The Reed–Frost chain-binomial epidemic in a small group: generation by generation, each susceptible escapes each case independently with probability 1 − p, so the next generation's cases are Binomial(S, 1 − (1 − p)^C). Left, a set of simulated outbreaks as lines of people infected so far against generation — grey the ones that fizzled, red the ones that took off — and the expected (average) path; right, the EXACT distribution of the final number infected as sideways bars on the same axis, split at its dip into "fizzles" and "takes off" with each one's probability. Choose this scene for ANY request about the Reed–Frost model, chain binomial, stochastic or random outbreaks, why some outbreaks die out while others explode, minor versus major outbreaks, extinction probability, or an outbreak in a household, class, ship or village. Give R0 or p: R0 ≈ p·(N − 1). p, r0, population and seed animate (seed in whole steps draws new outbreaks; the same seed always draws the same ones). Paused, the viewer scrubs or taps N, p and R0 in the header, and taps "new runs" for another set. Values: {reed_frost.r0}, {reed_frost.p}, {reed_frost.p_minor} and {reed_frost.p_major} (% exact; absent with {reed_frost.split} 0, a small group near threshold whose totals have no dip to split at — then all is one colour and neither side is named), {reed_frost.p_minor_bp} (% by the branching-process approximation), {reed_frost.p_no_spread} (% that the first case infects nobody), {reed_frost.mean_final} and {reed_frost.mean_major} (people), {reed_frost.cutoff}, {reed_frost.runs_major} and {reed_frost.runs_minor} (of the drawn runs), {reed_frost.expected_1} {reed_frost.expected_2} (expected new cases in generation 1, 2).
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "population": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "People in the group, N, 2–100 (default 30), the first cases included."
  },
  "p": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "The chance that one case infects one given susceptible in a generation, 0–1. Wins over r0."
  },
  "r0": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Instead of p: the expected cases one case causes in a group with no immunity, p = r0/(N − 1) (default 2)."
  },
  "initial": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "Cases in generation 0 (default 1)."
  },
  "runs": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "Simulated outbreaks drawn, 0–40 (default 12)."
  },
  "seed": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "Which random outbreaks (default 1). The same seed draws the same ones; animate it in whole steps for new ones."
  },
  "generations": {
   "type": "integer",
   "description": "Generations on the axis (default fitted). Give it when you animate p, r0 or population, so the axis holds still."
  },
  "show_expected": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "The dashed average path (default true)."
  },
  "show_distribution": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "The exact final-size bars on the right (default true)."
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- n_value: the N = 30 readout in the header
- p_value: the p = 0.069 readout
- r0_value: the R₀ ≈ 2 readout
- rerun: the new runs button (a tap draws new outbreaks)
- axes: the axes: generation, and infected so far (0 to N)
- run_<k>: the k-th simulated outbreak, k = 1…runs (group runs; runs_minor and runs_major split them)
- expected: the dashed average path (drawn with its label expected_label)
- cutoff: the dashed line across the bars between the fizzled totals and the ones that took off
- dist_minor: the bars of the final totals that count as fizzling (all the bars when there is no split)
- dist_major: the bars of the totals that count as taking off
- dist_axis: the distribution panel's base line, with its caption
- minor_label: the fizzles 21% label (drawn with dist_minor)
- major_label: the takes off 79% label (drawn with dist_major)
Examples:
Request: "Why do some outbreaks fizzle out while others explode?" → params: {"population":30,"r0":2,"runs":12}
Request: "Show the Reed–Frost chain binomial model for a household of 5 with p = 0.3." → params: {"population":5,"p":0.3,"runs":10}

Viewer can: Scrub N, p or R0; tap 'new runs' for fresh outbreaks under the same rule.

In YAML: `template: reed_frost` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
